newsitem.title: USA: GM still sees 15.3 mln-unit '97 U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: GM still sees 15.3 mln-unit '97 U.S. market.

text.p: General Motors Corp chairman and chief executive Jack Smith said Friday the automaker still expects the total U.S. market for cars and trucks to be about 15.3 million units for 1997.

"We have consistently thought the market would run somewhere about 15.3 million units and we still feel that that's the way it's going to run," Smith told Reuters following a presentation at a National Rainbow/PUSH Coalition conference here.
Smith noted that this would be the fourth consecutive year that U.S. car and truck sales exceeded 15 million units.
He said that, in the present economy, there is a good chance sales could run above 15 million units again in 1998.

"I would think, as of the moment, as we look at where the economy is running, that that's certainly a very strong possibility, that the market will continue to run over 15 million units again next year," Smith said.

Factors driving sales include high employment, low inflation, strong consumer confidence and the balanced budget agreement, said Smith, who participated in a panel discussion here on minority involvement in the auto industry.
Panel discussion covered manufacturers' efforts to increase minority suppliers and dealers, and other issues.
